name: Adenosine
high_alert_note: Not confirmed as high-alert on a source read; the institution's list governs.
summary: Intravenous antiarrhythmic used to convert paroxysmal supraventricular tachycardia to sinus rhythm. Nursing focus: heart block and asystole, resuscitative readiness and the very short action of the drug.
evidence_type_note: The evidence here is a regulator product label (prescribing information written for prescribers and pharmacists). It is not a bedside nursing practice guideline: the nursing actions are inferences from label warnings, marked partial, and the unit's protocol governs practice.
jurisdiction_note: US FDA label only. EMA, MHRA and SFDA labels were not read; indications, warnings and presentations differ by country and by manufacturer.

items.text: The label indicates intravenous adenosine for conversion to sinus rhythm of paroxysmal supraventricular tachycardia, including that associated with accessory bypass tracts, when appropriate vagal manoeuvres have not been effective.
Appropriate resuscitative measures should be available when the drug is given.
Continuous ECG monitoring and recording during administration follow the unit's protocol.
Adenosine decreases conduction through the AV node and may produce short-lasting first-, second- or third-degree heart block.
Patients who develop high-level block on one dose should not be given additional doses (a prescriber decision).
Transient or prolonged episodes of asystole have been reported, some fatal, and ventricular fibrillation has rarely been reported.
Because of the very short half-life, effects are generally self-limiting.
Facial flushing was the most frequently reported reaction in the controlled trials the label summarises, with headache and sweating also reported.
Call for help immediately for prolonged asystole, high-level heart block or ventricular fibrillation.
Record the rhythm strip, the response and any adverse event per unit standard.
Institution-specific preparation: follow your pharmacy's preparation standard and the product labelling. This library gives no preparation or concentration instructions.
Institution-specific dosing: follow the prescriber's order and your institution's approved protocol. This library gives no dosing instructions.

monitoring.text: Keep resuscitation equipment and trained staff immediately available.
Watch the ECG continuously for heart block or asystole.
Note flushing, headache or chest discomfort.
Call for help immediately for prolonged asystole or a dangerous rhythm.
Record the rhythm strip and response.
